findings.note: eip7702-unprotected-entrypoint: EIP-7702 unprotected entrypoint: DelegateContractV0.execute(DelegateContractV0.Call[]) (src/DelegateContractV0.sol#17-24) makes an arbitrary external call without checking msg.sender -- any caller can drive the delegated account.

eip7702-constructor-state: EIP-7702 constructor-only state: DelegateContractV1.guardians (src/DelegateContractV1.sol#23) is set only in a constructor of DelegateContractV1 (src/DelegateContractV1.sol#10-58) -- it will be zero for any account that delegates to this contract (the constructor never runs for the delegating EOA). Initialize it in a guarded initializer instead.

eip7702-storage-collision: EIP-7702 non-namespaced storage: DelegateContractV1 (src/DelegateContractV1.sol#10-58) declares 1 plain storage variable(s) and is delegate-shaped -- if this account re-delegates to a different implementation the slots can collide. Consider ERC-7201 namespaced storage.

eip7702-recallable-initializer: EIP-7702 re-callable initializer: DelegateContractV2.initialize(address[]) (src/DelegateContractV2.sol#31-39) sets DelegateContractV2.guardians (src/DelegateContractV2.sol#25) with no working one-shot guard -- anyone can (re-)initialize the delegated account and seize it.

eip7702-missing-nonce: EIP-7702 missing replay protection: DelegateContractV3.initialize(address[],uint8,bytes32,bytes32) (src/DelegateContractV3.sol#41-57) recovers a signature but tracks no nonce -- it can be replayed against the delegated account.

eip7702-replay-unsafe-sig: EIP-7702 chain-replayable signature: DelegateContractV3.initialize(address[],uint8,bytes32,bytes32) (src/DelegateContractV3.sol#41-57) recovers a signature whose digest binds neither block.chainid nor an EIP-712 domain separator -- it can be replayed on another chain/deployment.
